title: GraphSkill: Documentation-Guided Agentic Hierarchical Retrieval-Augmented Coding for Complex Graph Reasoning

problem.claim: Automated graph algorithm reasoning is an increasingly important application for large language models.

gap.claim: Existing approaches use flat technical-documentation retrieval that causes noisy retrieval and focus debugging on runtime errors while overlooking logical errors.

contributions.claim: GraphSkill is an agentic hierarchical retrieval-augmented coding framework using top-down document traversal, early pruning, and iterative self-debugging with automatically generated small-scale test cases.
ComplexGraph is a dataset covering small-scale, large-scale, and composite graph reasoning tasks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly propose GraphSkill and introduce the ComplexGraph dataset as responses to the identified limitations and evaluation needs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report higher task accuracy and lower inference cost than baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Automated graph algorithm reasoning is attracting increasing attention in the LLM community.
Existing methods separate task descriptions from graph data, generate documentation-augmented executable code, and refine it through debugging.
Existing methods overlook document hierarchy during retrieval and logical errors during debugging.
GraphSkill addresses these limitations with hierarchical retrieval, early pruning, and test-case-driven self-debugging.
The paper introduces ComplexGraph and reports improved accuracy and reduced inference cost against baselines.

source_observation.claim: Retrieval that models technical documentation hierarchy with top-down traversal and early pruning is presented as a way to address noisy retrieval.

interpretation.claim: Structured retrieval may improve the relevance of documentation used for code generation.

application.claim: For documentation-grounded coding systems, represent document structure explicitly and prune irrelevant branches early.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether hierarchical retrieval helps across domains beyond complex graph reasoning.

source_observation.claim: The proposed debugging agent generates small-scale test cases and iteratively refines code, while the reported evaluation shows higher accuracy and lower inference cost than baselines.

interpretation.claim: Test-case-driven self-debugging may address logical errors that runtime-error-focused debugging misses.

application.claim: Coding agents should use automatically generated tests to probe logical correctness during iterative refinement.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the test-generation procedure, error coverage, or whether the reported gains isolate self-debugging from the retrieval changes.

unknowns: Baseline identities, dataset sizes, task distributions, and numerical accuracy and cost results are unspecified.
The abstract does not describe the document hierarchy, pruning criteria, test-generation procedure, or agent architecture in detail.
The abstract does not provide independent verification or reproducibility details.
